state: template. Main fills every null once the four fixture pull requests exist and the controller is merged, checks each expected_event_digest with analyze.py digest against the shakedown's metadata step, and hashes this file after the shakedown. It changes afterwards only for a recorded protocol defect, never after a measured round.

PY.packaging: the published Python composite action, v1.0.0

RS.packaging: Rust composite action with four native platform artifacts

TS-H.packaging: Node 24 action with a native Git supervisor, not a pure TypeScript action

runtime.note: Filled from the shakedown, per architecture: the runner image name and version from the log's 'Runner Image' group, the PY python3 --version line, the git version line, the RS and TS-H identity lines (the TS-H one with its Node version written as 'node <node>'), and the Node version TS-H executed. Any measured job that differs is drift and closes the attempt; a job whose log shows no image, image version or TS-H Node version is a protocol deviation. The runner version is recorded per job but not frozen, since the design names it as a record only.

schedule.rotation: int(SHA256(ASCII 'E2E3-v1|20260929|<workload>'), big endian) mod 3, an offset into A, B, C
schedule.dispatch: one labeled event per round, one round at a time, cycles W3, W1, W2, W4; record the actual order

estimators.primary: Jobs API completed_at - started_at of attempt 1, whole seconds
estimators.bootstrap_rejection: a digest, read as a big-endian integer, at or above floor(2^256/12)*12 is rejected and '<key>|<counter>' hashed instead, counter 1, 2, ...; the accepted value mod 12 is the round index
estimators.bootstrap_unit: whole rounds: the six jobs of one dispatch, both architectures, resampled together
estimators.private_billing: CEIL(duration / 60) per job before pairing, over the job's precision interval, at least one minute for a job that ran; AMBIGUOUS where the interval crosses a 60-second boundary, never a saving

log_spans.T_span: first to last timestamped line of the job log
log_spans.T_download: 'Getting action download info' to 'Complete job name'
log_spans.T_metadata: the metadata step's group line to the variant step's group line
log_spans.T_action: the variant step's group line to 'Post job cleanup.' or 'Cleaning up orphan processes'
log_spans.T_post: that line to the last line

failure_accounting: Only attempt 1 counts. Rerun attempts are recorded and excluded, and never replace a round.
A round counts only when all six of its jobs are valid and the twelve other jobs were skipped.
W4's exit 1 is its expected result; a W4 success is a candidate defect.

A candidate defect, a protocol deviation, runtime or table drift, or an operator cancel after the first measured dispatch closes the attempt incomplete. A successor needs a new, separately approved preregistration.

An infrastructure failure discards the whole round for all variants. One replacement of the same workload and order is appended; at most three in total. It is eligible only when the variant never started, by both the Jobs API steps and the log, and the job's terminal ##[error] line or a failure-level check-run annotation, all pages of which were kept, names a provider cause by infrastructure_evidence, while nothing matches a candidate pattern. The job's image, when its log shows one, must still be the frozen image.

A failure before the variant started whose records match a candidate pattern (the candidate's own reference failing to resolve or its package failing to load) is a candidate defect and never enters the replacement pool.
Any other failure before the variant started, including a failed set-up or a missing log without provider evidence, is ambiguous.
An ambiguous cause pauses the series for review, which then closes the attempt rather than relabel it.

Every dispatch, shakedown, measured or replacement, is a distinct run. The ledger lists them in the order the runs were created, and each run is created only after the jobs of the one before it ended.
base_tip_before and base_tip_after of every dispatch must equal the frozen base.

infrastructure_evidence.note: Python regular expressions for a job that failed before its variant started, checked against actions/runner v2.337.0, commit 397b032cbf865e9c3ddfab89d533ec19325e1273. terminal_error is matched only against the job's last ##[error] line, annotation only against failure-level check-run annotations; candidate against every log line and annotation, and a candidate match wins. A provider failure counts only when the terminal cause itself names it. Retry warnings (ActionManager.cs:1743, 1747, 1760) and the generic 'Failed to download archive ... after N attempts' wrapper (:1769, which also wraps a 404 whose inner cause only debug output shows) are never provider evidence. Sources: download timeout, ActionManager.cs:1723 wrapped at :1769 and printed as the inner message by InfrastructureError at :131; HTTP 5xx, EnsureSuccessStatusCode at :1710 after the retries, the inner HttpRequestException message printed at :131 (its text is .NET's System.Net.Http, not runner source); shutdown, JobRunner.cs:133 and :136, logged as an error issue at :141. 'lost communication with the server' is GitHub's server-side annotation for a lost hosted runner and is not in runner source. Candidate: ActionManager.cs:912 and :1544, :1697, ActionNotFoundException.cs:32 and :35, ActionManifestManager.cs:147; the remaining two are GitHub's server-side resolution messages. Frozen with the contract; confirmed or extended only before the hash, never after a measured round.
